findings: Resolved the fixed local source and verified its 34-page count and hash against the previous audit and register. The source identifies Richard Nickl and arXiv:2210.13008v3, stamped 27 January 2024. Textual equality with the journal typesetting is not asserted.

Extracted all 34 pages afresh and enumerated actual joined small-cap Theorem heading lines. The inventory contains exactly Theorems 1-12, on pages 3,4,6,6,7,7,8,9,12,12,17,25. The source contents and page-13 heading identify Proofs as numbered main Section 3, so Theorems 11 and 12 remain included. References end on page 34; there is no attached appendix.

Compared all twelve complete statements with the rendered PDF. None crosses a page boundary. Introductory Theorems 1 and 2 remain separate from the later detailed theorems, and external theorem citations, propositions, lemmas and unlabelled consequences do not enter the theorem inventory.

Theorem 1 retains positive C2 coefficients, agreement near the boundary and equality of transition operators at some fixed positive time. Theorem 2 retains its broadly worded regularity and appropriate-prior clauses, with the explicit source reference to Theorems 9/10 recorded separately for their detailed resolution.

Theorem 2 uses the nonlinear link evaluated at the posterior mean of theta. It does not use the posterior mean of f. The original theorem claims consistency for each fixed t>0, without an unconditional algebraic rate or a spectral-condition assumption.

Theorem 3 retains the chosen estimator (63), its J_N order, combined C2/Hs bound and L2 operator norm. Theorem 4 retains its existential domain, all-estimator infimum, printed Hs-ball supremum, H2 operator loss, exponent and liminf lower bound. The estimator (63) and geometric lower-bound construction are not imposed on every estimator in Theorem 4.

Theorem 5 retains the complete pairwise positivity, compact-interior agreement and C2 norm-sum assumptions, logarithmic modulus and injectivity conclusion. Theorems 6 and 7 inherit those clauses. Their additional Hs bound and first-eigenspace condition remain distinct, and the exact gamma reference to (12) is archived with its qualifications.

Both parts of Theorem 8 match: the enlarged hyperrectangle, w>=2, sufficiently large m, simple first positive eigenvalue, compact subsets of the original rectangle, and the perturbation by f0 with Hs bound and small supremum distance to one. A reference to condition (10) does not import all pairwise hypotheses of Theorem 6.

Theorem 9 retains the smoothness threshold, strict truth lower bound, smaller support set O00, explicit posterior/prior references, K order and posterior operator-error event. Theorem 10 retains both posterior conclusions, logarithmic baseline and optional algebraic rate. The following source paragraph explicitly restricts condition (10) to f0, not every prior draw.

Theorem 11 retains its Proposition 2B reference, compact-interior agreement, constant dependencies and chained KL/HS/compact-support-dual bound. The opening C1/positivity requirements and branch-B Hs bound were checked on page 14 and recorded separately for each coefficient, without replacing them by a norm-sum or stronger C2 hypothesis.

Theorem 12 retains the general prior sequence, small-ball mass, sieve mass, both testing errors, separate delta_N and bar-delta_N sequences, B>A+2 and 0<b<B-A-2. Its conclusion retains the sieve intersection and exponential O_P remainder. It does not require the specific Gaussian prior or a particular test implementation.

Checked all sixteen original source entries against their defining passages: reflected SDE and reflection terms, domain, Neumann generator and transition kernel, eigen-pairs, compact-support spaces, general parameter space and Bayes formula, cutoff Gaussian series and transformed prior, estimator matrix, first eigenspace, enlarged rectangle, KL divergence, KL neighborhood and condition (10).

The Gaussian series has indices 0 through K and two nested compact support sets; the estimator uses indices 0 through J-1. The estimator matrix and its full-space zero extension match (62)-(63). The subsequent one-sided compression description remains archived as a source discrepancy rather than substituted for the definition.

The neighborhood B_delta on page 25 prints identical p_(D,f) terms in its variance ratio. The immediately following proof prints f0 in the denominator instead. Both passages are retained, with the discrepancy explicit; the original neighborhood used by Theorem 12 is not silently repaired.

Reviewed all nineteen auxiliary passages and sixteen source notes. These preserve Lebesgue/volume conventions, fixed observation spacing, norms, inherited theorem hypotheses, Proposition 2B, first-eigenspace exponent, general-prior reset, inverse link, posterior-mean interpretation and the truth-only spectral condition. No external appendix or proof source was consulted.

The enlarged-rectangle smoothness assertion, volume-normalization conflict, Theorem 4 estimator-domain issue, Theorem 11 regularity scope and logarithmic endpoint convention remain explicit source limitations. Census validation does not certify the mathematical claims or repair these ambiguities.

Reviewed the 45 direct dependencies and recursive source graph, giving 85 deduplicated theorem connections. The specific estimator is related only to Theorem 3; the geometric enlargement only to Theorem 8; the KL neighborhood only to Theorem 12. The general-prior theorem does not acquire Gaussian-series or spectral-condition dependencies.

Checked every natural-language source keyword, naming passage and highlight selector. Condition (10) remains a theorem excerpt, the state-domain requirements remain a condition, and diffusion-model prose remains a source passage. Names and explanatory paths do not replace original statements.

All six content JSON files passed review unchanged. Archived the previous scripts and retained an empty-directory rebuild using the verified local PDF. Inherited-hypothesis passages now read the saved in-script theorem declarations rather than performing file I/O during import. All six artifacts reproduced byte for byte; source-review records were preserved.
Independent validators check inventory identity, schema and graph consistency after the manual source comparison. The saved evidence and findings describe a statement census, not proof certification.
